where: Section 1, the sentence beginning 'For ice melting ΔV'
problem: The sentence is broken: 'For ice melting ΔV Chapter 4.3).' Words, the sign of ΔV, the conclusion about the slope, and the opening parenthesis of the chapter link are all missing. A student cannot read what the chapter concludes for melting, and the broken line looks like a printing fault.
fix: For ice melting, ΔV = V_liquid − V_solid < 0, so dP_sat/dT < 0: the melting point falls as pressure rises. This is why ice skates on a thin water film under pressure (see Chapter 4.3).

problem: The declared y range is 10 to 13, but the plotted line reaches ln(P/Pa) = 9.966 at 1/T = 0.003, so the end of the line falls outside the box and is clipped.
fix: Set the y-axis minimum to 9.9 (range 9.9 to 12.5), or cut the x range at 0.00298, so the whole line lies inside the axes.

problem: 'Gives a wrong sign or size' is loose. Using Celsius in this temperature range keeps the sign of (1/T2 − 1/T1) and of ln(P2/P1) the same; the real damage is a badly wrong magnitude. A sign flip needs negative Celsius values, which is a special case.
fix: Using T in °C. The equation needs kelvin; a Celsius value makes 1/T and ΔH/R(1/T2 − 1/T1) the wrong size, so the estimated pressure is badly wrong.
